name: write_unaligned
declaration: const unsafe fn write_unaligned (self , val : T) where T : Sized ,
documentation:
Overwrites a memory location with the given value without reading or
 dropping the old value.

 Unlike `write`, the pointer may be unaligned.

 See [`ptr::write_unaligned`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::write_unaligned`]: crate::ptr::write_unaligned()
rules: For safety, self must be valid for writes of a value of type T.
self need not be aligned for T when calling write_unaligned.
Overwriting the contents of self without dropping the old value is safe, even though it may leak allocations or resources.

When creating self as a pointer to an unaligned packed-struct field, use &raw mut rather than creating an intermediate reference and casting it to a raw pointer; creating the unaligned reference causes immediate undefined behavior, even if the reference is temporary and immediately cast.
